Of the 2 patterns, the closest to it is '^%{WORD:outcome} password for (?:invalid user )?%{NOTSPACE:user} from %{IP:src_ip} port %{INT:src_port} ssh2$'. the pattern matches up to %{NOTSPACE:user}, which fails on 'user nuno from 172.21.0.3 port 36658'. %{WORD} matches letters, digits and underscore only - NOT a dot, hyphen, colon or slash. For a hostname use %{HOSTNAME}, for any run of non-space characters use %{NOTSPACE} It also misses lines of other shapes: 'Invalid user operator from 172.21.0.3 port 58444'; 'Invalid user git from 172.21.0.3 port 58468'. If this line is a VARIANT of the others - an extra word, a field that is sometimes absent - make that part optional with (?:...)? rather than writing a second pattern. If it is a DIFFERENT KIND of message - different words, not one more of them - add a pattern for it to `alternatives`, reusing the same capture name for the same value.

The first it misses is '<81>1 2026-10-19T23:41:35.362212+00:00 web01 sudo - - -     sofia : user NOT in sudoers ; PWD=/home/sofia ; USER=root ; COMMAND=/usr/bin/apt-get update'. Of the 2 patterns, the closest to it is '(?<=<38>1 )%{TIMESTAMP_ISO8601:timestamp} %{HOSTNAME:host} sshd %{POSINT:pid} - -  %{DATA:message}'. the pattern matches up to %{TIMESTAMP_ISO8601:timestamp}, which fails on '<81>1 2026-10-19T23:41:35.362212+00:00 w' It also misses lines of other shapes: '<35>1 2026-10-19T23:41:31.111811+00:00 web01 sshd 33 - -  error: kex_exchange_identification: Connection closed by remote host'; '<85>1 2026-10-19T23:41:32.567584+00:00 web01 sudo - - -       ana : PWD=/home/ana ; USER=root ; COMMAND=/usr/bin/id'. If this line is a VARIANT of the others - an extra word, a field that is sometimes absent - make that part optional with (?:...)? rather than writing a second pattern. If it is a DIFFERENT KIND of message - different words, not one more of them - add a pattern for it to `alternatives`, reusing the same capture name for the same value.

findings.message: 'PORT', 'PROGRAM' are not grok patterns. Logstash refuses to compile an unknown name, so the filter never registers and EVERY line fails to parse - not just the ones this capture touches. Use a defined pattern: NUMBER or BASE10NUM for a decimal, HOSTNAME for a domain, NOTSPACE for anything without a space.
